selection: Fixed before optimization. Keep close variants (2mm/3mm, correlation/covariance, LU/LUDCMP, Jacobi 1d/2d, SYRK/SYR2K) together. Optimization covers dense products, matrix/vector algebra, factorization, statistics, recursive filtering, recurrence, dynamic programming and in-place stencils; holdout covers different programs using overlapping techniques. All original baseline timings were already public, so this is not a blind experiment or proof of generalization to arbitrary applications.
procedure: Keep all thirty Mech programs, inputs, C flags, finite limits and comparison tolerances fixed.
Investigate profiles and per-case candidate timing only on the optimization set.
Freeze the compiler candidate and its source fingerprint before holdout timing. Correctness checks may run on all programs throughout.
Report holdout results even if they regress. Do not select or retune the same candidate using holdout per-case performance.
Future rounds reuse this split and disclose previous holdout exposure; a new application is needed for a fresh external validation.
Commit compiler changes and experiment receipts only to the PR #1001 branch codex/polybench-native-matrices.

measurements.timing_boundaries: Reuse baseline checked Mech timing and separate C kernel/fresh-allocation timings; parsing, JIT compilation and input import are excluded.
measurements.correctness: Check all finite C live-outs with rtol=1e-10 and atol=1e-9. Original/decoded artifacts, Object emission, alias safety, resource denial/recovery and compression regressions remain required.

aggregate_metrics.primary: Equal-weight geometric mean of baseline Mech time / candidate Mech time, separately for optimization, holdout and all thirty kernels.
aggregate_metrics.c_comparison: Equal-weight geometric mean of Mech/C runtime ratios for kernel-only and fresh allocation/copy comparisons, kept separate.
also_report: number of kernels over 5% slower than baseline
number of kernels faster than C
sum of per-kernel median Mech times (secondary; workload dependent)
aggregate_metrics.exclusions: No silent removal of slow, failed or incorrect cases. A missing case makes an aggregate incomplete; a correctness failure invalidates the candidate.
